hold_text: TWO SEPARATE REASONS THIS CANNOT SELF-LAND, and they must not be collapsed — the tier one is the binding one. (1) TIER-2 BY PATH. The diff touches src/runtime/manager_status.py and src/web/api/routers/work.py, and this guard names both under the src/** rule. ⚠️ THIS FILE ORIGINALLY DECLARED TIER 1 AND THAT WAS WRONG. The MI-238 checklist row argues `why_it_is_tier_1` from CONTENT (a read-only GET, no order path, no risk cap, no new write surface) and that content argument is CORRECT and unchanged — but the repo's tier rule is by PATH, and a change to the running web-api service is Tier-2 whatever the route does. Field beats comment: the guard is the field and the item's prose is a claim about it. Recorded rather than quietly corrected, because a session reading the checklist row alone would make the same mistake. (2) THE QUEUE IS HELD for #11640, declared by the manager when this session was spawned, so no auto-merge arming file ships here even once the tier question is settled. ⚠️ NO NEW WRITE SURFACE IS ADDED: the decision inbox's write route (POST /api/bot/work/decision) is token-gated and fail-closed today and is byte-for-byte unchanged. ⚠️ WHAT A HUMAN SHOULD ACTUALLY READ HERE IS THE ONE BEHAVIOUR CHANGE, which is NOT the new route — a new route serves nobody until a consumer calls it. It is that the Telegram /status readout changes, because build_sections now reads an item's status through the ONE merge owner instead of item['state'] directly. MEASURED 2026-09-10 over all 244 items of MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json: 65 rows carry `status` and NO `state`, and nothing in this repo reads `status` on this file (manager_status.build_sections and scripts/ops/manager_view.py both key on `state` alone), so those 65 rows previously landed in no section of /status at all and surfaced only as `(no state) 65` in the counts line. They now render. The counts section also gains three terse lines: a status-basis breakdown, a state-vs-status disagreement count, and the population line naming how many rows NO section covers (18 of 238 on main). That is strictly more information inside the same 4096-char budget, and tests/test_manager_status.py's cap and degradation-ladder tests pass unchanged. ⚠️ THOSE LINES WERE CUT DOWN AFTER A FIRST DRAFT BROKE A BUDGET TEST: ~450 characters of full explanation pushed the omission FOOTER itself over the cap under a tight budget, i.e. the readout blinding itself to what it had dropped. The explanations moved to the page, which has no character budget — that split is much of the argument for the page existing, and the fix was to the code, not to the test.
why: MI-238, operator-directed 2026-09-10: the manager checklist becomes a live Workflow page on the SPA with collapsible rows and the open-decision list, so the operator can track session progress without pulling detail into chat. Three halves. (1) BOT ROUTE — GET /api/bot/work/checklist on the EXISTING work router, serving docs/claude/work/MANAGER-CHECKLIST.json THROUGH src/runtime/manager_status.py's existing grading. Nothing is built from scratch: manager_status already read the checklist and already owned grade_owner/build_sections/StatusReadout, and work.py already served GET /api/bot/work/decisions, so the decisions half needed no new route at all. Both premises were re-verified in this session rather than inherited from the brief. (2) THE ONE-OWNER RULE, which is the design decision the whole item turns on — the file carries TWO competing status fields and the SPA must not merge them itself. Re-MEASURED here rather than re-quoted (MI-237's 177/83 was taken on a smaller file): over all 244 items, 179 carry `state`, 83 carry `status`, 18 carry both and 13 of those DISAGREE, four reading `state: in_flight` against `status: done`. manager_status.effective_state is now the single owner; `state` wins a disagreement precisely BECAUSE it is what every existing consumer reads, so the page agrees with manager_view.py and the manager guards by construction rather than by coincidence, and a disagreement is REPORTED (basis `disagree`, flagged inline) rather than silently resolved. Five never-collapsed bases ship with every row and are registered with collapsed-state-guard as manager_status.status_basis — `undeclared` is kept apart although measured at ZERO, because a state measured at zero is not a state that cannot occur. MI-237 is deliberately NOT a blocked_on edge: the two are order-independent given the single owner, and a false blocker is worse than a missing one. (3) FRESHNESS STATED, NOT PROMISED AROUND — the route reads the VM's WORKING TREE, which ict-git-sync pulls roughly every 5 minutes, so the page is exactly as fresh as the last PUSH plus that interval and a manager must push the checklist BEFORE answering a status request. read_file_commit gives the checklist its OWN as-of stamp (last commit sha, time, age, and whether the working tree matches it) beside the existing whole-tree provenance, because a tree can be perfectly `synced` while the checklist on it is three hours old. `workingTreeDirty` is null when unread, never false. A frozen page reading byte-identically to a live one is the coordination board's 2026-09-07 failure, and _freshness_warnings branches on every tree and commit state so each condition announces itself. TESTS: 31 new, and the suite is MUTATION-TESTED rather than assumed load-bearing — collapsing status_only back into `no status` (the exact regression that drops the 65 rows) fails three of them. The freshness tests carry a positive control in both directions: a clean tree must produce ZERO warnings, or `no warnings` would be evidence of nothing. 119 pass across the four affected modules. NOT IN THIS DIFF: the SPA page itself, which lives in benbaichmankass/ict-trader-dashboard and ships as its own PR.
